source.title: Dendritic In-Context Learning in a Single-Layer Spiking Neural Network
source.authors: Juwei Shen; Yu-Jie Wu; Chang-Wen Chen

page_placements.theme: Shape of toy ICL transitions depends on parametrisation, initialisation, task and data size

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites prior reports of induction-head emergence and compares them analogically with its own grokking-like ICL results, but does not measure induction heads or test their role.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own ICL performance and training-transition results, but not induction-head formation, induction behavior, or a contemporaneous training-loss bump. Its statement about induction-head emergence is attributed to cited work, not reported as a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study trains a 4-layer Transformer (with MLPs) on Garg linear-regression ICL and reports eval R2. It never measures induction heads, previous-token heads, induction scores, loss bumps or head ablations. Its one sentence on induction-head emergence is an analogy to cited work (Olsson et al. 2022; Edelman et al. 2024), not a result of this study. Its grokking-like eval-R2 jumps are a related but different construct: transitions in regression ICL accuracy with no circuit identified.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that DendriCL's apical compartment implements leaky online LMS (linear-probe R2 = 0.93) and solves Garg ICL for d from 5 to 50 with frozen weights, training smoothly and stably across seeds. Dense Transformers are near-Bayes at d≤25, show grokking-like trimodal seed outcomes at d=30, and fail at chance for d≥40 despite 5× compute. The authors call the d≥40 failure architectural rather than budget-induced.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply an induction-head measurement method; it studies ICL in a compartmental spiking architecture and reports Transformer ICL comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports Transformer ICL outcomes varying with task dimension, training budget, and seed; it does not assess induction-head sensitivity to these conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: A 4-layer, 1.0M-parameter Transformer on Garg linear-regression ICL succeeds at d=25 (R2 0.991 ± 0.002, 50k steps). At d=30 it is seed-dependent: 3 of 6 seeds fail, 1 is partial, 2 jump abruptly to R2 ≈ 0.98. At d≥40 it fails at chance (R2 ≤ 0.009) even with 5× compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer acquisition of regression-style ICL shows abrupt, seed-dependent, grokking-like transitions whose success probability falls with task dimension.

record.problems: The study does not measure induction heads or their mechanism. Its induction-head statement is attributed to cited work. The Transformer grokking analysis is limited to 6 seeds at d=30, as the authors note.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible induction-head results were reported. Other ICL benchmark results are outside the claim versions except for the seed-level Transformer d=30 findings recorded above.

untested.parts: No induction or previous-token heads, and no composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour; the model is not attention-only.
No induction-head formation timing and no training-loss bump. Eval-R2 jumps on regression ICL are not linked to any circuit.
No measure of induction heads' share of ICL in large models.
No induction behaviour measured across families, sizes or runs.
Task dimension and compute are varied, but only ICL accuracy is reported. Induction-head formation is never measured.
No comparison of few-shot mechanisms with induction heads.
No sub-steps of induction-head formation measured.

record.verdict_notes: Do not count this study for V2 or V5: the Transformer here uses MLPs, and the task is continuous regression. The induction-head mention is a single analogical sentence citing prior work. The source is internally inconsistent on breakthrough steps: text says ~4000 and ~6000, Fig. 6 legend says 8k and 16k. Transformer baselines are the authors' own re-implementations.

versions.untested_parts: No induction heads, previous-token heads, or induction mechanism are measured.
The paper reports grokking-like changes in evaluation R2 for a Transformer, but does not measure induction-head emergence or a training-loss bump at the same time.
No induction-head contribution to most ICL in large Transformers is measured.
No cross-family or cross-run measurement of induction behavior is made.
The study varies ICL task dimensions and training setups, but does not measure whether or when induction heads form or whether their formation depends on those conditions.
No few-shot task-learning mechanism is compared with induction heads.
No induction-head formation sub-steps or multiple transitions are measured.

relation.reason: Section 5.2 draws an analogy between its Transformer grokking results and induction-head emergence in cited work; it neither tests nor uses induction heads.

tranche.reason: The study measures synthetic regression ICL and dendritic LMS dynamics, without measuring induction-head formation, composition, prevalence, or causal contribution. Its grokking results do not establish any induction-head claim version.

source_check.notes: The statement's R2 ≤ 0.009 holds for the reported means at tested d=40 and 50; Table 12 includes individual seeds at 0.010, contradicting the source's stronger all-seeds bound. Breakthrough times also conflict between Section 5.2 and Figure 6's legend; these inconsistencies do not affect the six checked values.
